Creating Beautiful Lollipop Charts with ggplot2

R
ggplot2
Data Visualization
Tutorial
A step-by-step guide to evolving a basic lollipop chart into an advanced, publication-ready visualization
Author

Your Name

Published

October 14, 2025

Introduction

In this tutorial, we’ll explore how to create increasingly sophisticated lollipop charts using ggplot2. We’ll start with a basic plot and progressively add elements to make it more informative and visually appealing.

Lollipop charts are excellent alternatives to bar charts when you want to emphasize individual data points while reducing visual clutter. They’re particularly effective for showing rankings, comparisons, or changes over categories.

We’ll use a dataset representing customer satisfaction scores across different service departments.

Setup

First, let’s load the required packages and prepare our data:

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)  # Includes ggplot2, dplyr, and other essential packages
library(scales)     # For formatting axes and labels

# Create sample data: customer satisfaction scores by department
data_satisfaction <- tibble(
  department = c("Sales", "Support", "Billing", "Technical", 
                 "Shipping", "Returns", "Quality", "Management"),
  score = c(78, 85, 72, 88, 80, 68, 82, 75),
  target = 80  # Company target score
)

# Preview the data
head(data_satisfaction)
# A tibble: 6 × 3
  department score target
  <chr>      <dbl>  <dbl>
1 Sales         78     80
2 Support       85     80
3 Billing       72     80
4 Technical     88     80
5 Shipping      80     80
6 Returns       68     80

Chart 1: Basic Lollipop Chart

Let’s start with a simple lollipop chart showing satisfaction scores by department.

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = department, y = score)) +  # Set up with x and y
  geom_segment(aes(x = department, xend = department,        # Draw vertical lines
                   y = 0, yend = score)) +
  geom_point(size = 4)                                       # Add points at top

Code Explanation

Line 1: ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = department, y = score)) - Initializes the plot with department on x-axis and satisfaction score on y-axis

Lines 2-3: geom_segment() creates vertical lines from y=0 to the score value for each department

Line 4: geom_point() adds circular points at the top of each line, creating the “lollipop” appearance

What we have so far: A functional but basic lollipop chart. The data is visible but the chart lacks color, proper ordering, context, and visual refinement.

Chart 2: Intermediate Enhancement

Now we’ll improve the chart by reordering, adding colors, including a target line, and applying a clean theme with better labels.

What we’re adding in this evolution:

  • Reordered departments by score for easier comparison
  • Color coding to distinguish above/below target
  • Horizontal orientation for better label readability
  • Target reference line showing company goal
  • Improved axis labels and title for clarity
  • Clean theme to remove visual clutter
  • Larger points for better visibility
# Add column for above/below target
data_satisfaction <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(
    performance = ifelse(score >= target, "Above Target", "Below Target"),
    performance = factor(performance, levels = c("Above Target", "Below Target"))
  )

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = reorder(department, score), y = score, 
                              color = performance)) +
  # Draw segments
  geom_segment(aes(x = reorder(department, score), 
                   xend = reorder(department, score),
                   y = 0, yend = score),
               linewidth = 1.5) +
  # Add points
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  # Add target reference line
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Flip coordinates for horizontal layout
  coord_flip() +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Above Target" = "#52A675", 
                                 "Below Target" = "#E76F51")) +
  # Format y-axis
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
                     limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Scores by Department",
    subtitle = "Dashed line shows company target (80 points)",
    x = "Department",
    y = "Satisfaction Score (0-100)",
    color = "Performance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

Code Explanation

Lines 2-6: Creates a new column performance categorizing departments as “Above Target” or “Below Target”

Lines 8-9: ggplot() with reorder(department, score) to sort departments by score, and color = performance for conditional coloring

Lines 11-15: geom_segment() creates vertical lines with increased thickness (linewidth = 1.5)

Line 17: geom_point() adds larger points (size = 5)

Lines 19-20: geom_hline() adds a dashed horizontal reference line at the target score (80)

Line 22: coord_flip() rotates the chart to horizontal orientation for better department name readability

Lines 24-25: scale_color_manual() applies green for above target and coral for below target

Lines 27-28: scale_y_continuous() sets axis breaks and limits

Lines 29-35: labs() adds descriptive title, subtitle explaining the target line, and clear axis labels

Line 36: theme_minimal() applies clean theme

Lines 37-40: theme() customizes title and legend position

What we have now: A much more informative chart with sorted departments, color-coded performance, and a clear target reference. The horizontal orientation and clean formatting make it presentation-ready.

Chart 3: Advanced Visualization

Let’s take it to the next level with enhanced styling, value labels, variance from target, and polished formatting suitable for publication.

What we’re adding in this final evolution:

  • Variance indicators showing distance from target
  • Value labels on each point
  • Segment styling from target line instead of zero
  • Enhanced color palette with gradient effect
  • Department rankings in labels
  • Summary statistics annotation
  • Enhanced typography with refined spacing
  • Data source caption for proper attribution
# Calculate variance from target and add rankings
target_value <- 80  # Store target as variable

data_satisfaction <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(
    variance = score - target_value,
    rank = rank(-score, ties.method = "first"),
    dept_label = paste0("#", rank, " ", department)
  )

# Calculate summary statistics
avg_score <- round(mean(data_satisfaction$score), 1)
above_target_pct <- round(sum(data_satisfaction$score >= target_value) / 
                          nrow(data_satisfaction) * 100, 0)

# Define enhanced color palette
perf_colors <- c("Above Target" = "#2E7D32", "Below Target" = "#C62828")

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = reorder(dept_label, score), y = score)) +
  # Draw segments from target line to score
  geom_segment(aes(x = reorder(dept_label, score), 
                   xend = reorder(dept_label, score),
                   y = target_value, yend = score,
                   color = performance),
               linewidth = 2,
               alpha = 0.8) +
  # Add target reference line
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_value, 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray30", 
             linewidth = 1) +
  # Add points with enhanced styling
  geom_point(aes(color = performance), 
             size = 6,
             alpha = 0.9) +
  # Add value labels
  geom_text(aes(label = score),
            hjust = -0.5,
            size = 3.5,
            fontface = "bold",
            color = "gray20") +
  # Add variance labels
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(variance >= 0, 
                                paste0("+", variance), 
                                as.character(variance))),
            hjust = 1.5,
            size = 3,
            color = "gray40") +
  # Flip coordinates
  coord_flip() +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_color_manual(values = perf_colors,
                     name = "vs Target (80)") +
  # Format x-axis (becomes y after flip)
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10),
                     limits = c(0, 95),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.15))) +
  # Add comprehensive labels
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Performance: 63% of Departments Meet Target",
    subtitle = "Technical leads with 88 points (+8 vs target) | Segments show variance from 80-point target",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Satisfaction Score (out of 100)",
    caption = "Data source: Q4 2024 Customer Satisfaction Survey | n = 1,247 responses | Visualization: Your Name"
  ) +
  # Add summary statistics as text annotation (no box, positioned at bottom right)
  annotate("text",
           x = 1, y = 90,
           label = paste0("Summary: Avg = ", avg_score, 
                         " | Above Target = ", above_target_pct, 
                         "% | Range = ", min(data_satisfaction$score), 
                         "-", max(data_satisfaction$score)),
           hjust = 0,
           size = 3.2,
           color = "gray30",
           fontface = "italic") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # Title and text styling
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16,
                              margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "#5A6C7D",
                                  lineheight = 1.3,
                                  margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#6C757D",
                                hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    
    # Axis styling
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold",
                              margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#2C3E50"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    
    # Legend styling
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    
    # Grid and panel styling
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#E9ECEF", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
    # Margins
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )

Code Explanation

Lines 2-7: Calculates variance from target, ranking, and creates department labels with rank numbers

Lines 10-12: Calculates summary statistics including average score and percentage above target

Line 15: Defines enhanced color palette with darker, more professional shades

Line 17: ggplot() with reordered department labels including rankings

Lines 19-26: geom_segment() creates segments that start at the target line (80) rather than zero, making variance immediately visible. Color coded by performance with increased thickness

Lines 28-31: geom_hline() adds prominent target reference line

Lines 33-35: geom_point() adds large colored points

Lines 37-41: geom_text() adds score value labels to the right of points

Lines 43-48: geom_text() adds variance labels (e.g., “+8” or “-12”) to the left of points

Line 50: coord_flip() for horizontal orientation

Lines 52-53: scale_color_manual() applies custom colors

Lines 55-57: scale_y_continuous() with expanded right margin for labels

Lines 59-65: labs() adds comprehensive labels including percentage meeting target in title, top performer in subtitle, and detailed caption

Lines 67-93: Multiple annotate() calls create a summary statistics box showing average, percentage above target, and score range

Lines 94-122: Comprehensive theme customization including enhanced typography, legend at top, grid customization, and proper margins

Final result: A publication-ready lollipop chart that clearly communicates satisfaction performance across departments. The segments starting from the target line, variance labels, ranking numbers, and summary statistics box create a comprehensive visualization suitable for executive presentations, reports, or dashboards.

Comparison: All Three Charts

Here’s a side-by-side view of our progression:

Aspect Basic Intermediate Advanced
Readability Poor (unsorted, vertical) Good (sorted, horizontal, colored) Excellent (all + rankings + variance)
Context None Title & target line Full context with summary stats
Visual Appeal Plain points and lines Color-coded with reference Enhanced colors + annotations
Data Layers Points only Points + target line Points + variance segments + labels
Statistical Info Visual values only Target comparison Variance, rankings, summary stats
Professional Use Not recommended Acceptable for internal use Publication-ready

Key Takeaways

Tip

Tips for Creating Better ggplot2 Lollipop Charts:

  1. Always reorder categories - Use reorder() to sort by value for easier visual comparison and pattern recognition

  2. Use horizontal orientation for long labels - Apply coord_flip() when category names are lengthy or numerous

  3. Start segments meaningfully - Instead of always starting at zero, consider starting from a baseline (like target or mean) to emphasize variance

  4. Add reference lines - Use geom_hline() or geom_vline() to show targets, averages, or thresholds

  5. Color with purpose - Use color to show categorical groups or highlight above/below threshold performance

  6. Label directly - Add value labels with geom_text() to reduce need for axis reading, especially with many categories

  7. Adjust segment thickness - Use linewidth = 1.5-2.5 for segments; too thin looks fragile, too thick looks heavy

  8. Mind the point size - Points should be 4-6 size units; large enough to see but not overwhelming

  9. Consider Cleveland dot plots - For comparing multiple groups, consider faceting or using geom_linerange() with two points

  10. Export at high resolution - Use ggsave("plot.png", width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300) for publication-quality images

Next Steps

Try applying these principles to other comparison visualizations:

  • Dumbbell plots for showing change between two time points
  • Slope charts for visualizing trends across categories
  • Dot plots with error bars for showing uncertainty
  • Cleveland dot plots for multi-group comparisons

Want to create grouped lollipop charts?

You can show multiple series with position dodging:

# Create data with two time periods
data_comparison <- data_satisfaction %>%
  select(department, score) %>%
  rename(current = score) %>%
  mutate(previous = current - sample(-5:8, n(), replace = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(current, previous), 
               names_to = "period", 
               values_to = "score")

# Create grouped lollipop chart
ggplot(data_comparison, 
       aes(x = reorder(department, score), 
           y = score, 
           color = period)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, 
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = department, 
                   y = 0, yend = score),
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
               linewidth = 1) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2C5F8D", "#E76F51"),
                     labels = c("Current Quarter", "Previous Quarter")) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Score Comparison",
       x = "Department",
       y = "Score",
       color = "Period") +
  theme_minimal()

This creates side-by-side lollipops showing changes over time.

Alternative: Dumbbell Chart

Here’s a bonus approach showing change between two points:

# Create before/after data
data_dumbbell <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(previous_score = score - sample(3:12, n(), replace = TRUE)) %>%
  select(department, previous_score, score, rank)

ggplot(data_dumbbell) +
  # Draw segments between points
  geom_segment(aes(x = previous_score, xend = score,
                   y = reorder(department, score), 
                   yend = reorder(department, score)),
               color = "gray70",
               linewidth = 2) +
  # Add previous period points
  geom_point(aes(x = previous_score, 
                 y = reorder(department, score)),
             color = "#E76F51",
             size = 5) +
  # Add current period points
  geom_point(aes(x = score, 
                 y = reorder(department, score)),
             color = "#52A675",
             size = 5) +
  # Add labels
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Improvement by Department",
    subtitle = "All departments showed improvement from Q3 to Q4 2024",
    x = "Satisfaction Score",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

## Introduction

In this tutorial, we'll explore how to create increasingly sophisticated lollipop charts using `ggplot2`. We'll start with a basic plot and progressively add elements to make it more informative and visually appealing.

Lollipop charts are excellent alternatives to bar charts when you want to emphasize individual data points while reducing visual clutter. They're particularly effective for showing rankings, comparisons, or changes over categories.

We'll use a dataset representing customer satisfaction scores across different service departments.

## Setup

First, let's load the required packages and prepare our data:

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)  # Includes ggplot2, dplyr, and other essential packages
library(scales)     # For formatting axes and labels

# Create sample data: customer satisfaction scores by department
data_satisfaction <- tibble(
  department = c("Sales", "Support", "Billing", "Technical", 
                 "Shipping", "Returns", "Quality", "Management"),
  score = c(78, 85, 72, 88, 80, 68, 82, 75),
  target = 80  # Company target score
)

# Preview the data
head(data_satisfaction)
```

---

## Chart 1: Basic Lollipop Chart

Let's start with a simple lollipop chart showing satisfaction scores by department.

```{r}
#| label: chart-basic
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = department, y = score)) +  # Set up with x and y
  geom_segment(aes(x = department, xend = department,        # Draw vertical lines
                   y = 0, yend = score)) +
  geom_point(size = 4)                                       # Add points at top
```

### Code Explanation

**Line 1:** `ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = department, y = score))` - Initializes the plot with department on x-axis and satisfaction score on y-axis

**Lines 2-3:** `geom_segment()` creates vertical lines from y=0 to the score value for each department

**Line 4:** `geom_point()` adds circular points at the top of each line, creating the "lollipop" appearance

::: {.highlight-box .info}
**What we have so far:**
A functional but basic lollipop chart. The data is visible but the chart lacks color, proper ordering, context, and visual refinement.
:::

---

## Chart 2: Intermediate Enhancement

Now we'll improve the chart by reordering, adding colors, including a target line, and applying a clean theme with better labels.

::: {.highlight-box .warning}
**What we're adding in this evolution:**

- **Reordered departments** by score for easier comparison
- **Color coding** to distinguish above/below target
- **Horizontal orientation** for better label readability
- **Target reference line** showing company goal
- **Improved axis labels** and title for clarity
- **Clean theme** to remove visual clutter
- **Larger points** for better visibility

:::

```{r}
#| label: chart-intermediate
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

# Add column for above/below target
data_satisfaction <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(
    performance = ifelse(score >= target, "Above Target", "Below Target"),
    performance = factor(performance, levels = c("Above Target", "Below Target"))
  )

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = reorder(department, score), y = score, 
                              color = performance)) +
  # Draw segments
  geom_segment(aes(x = reorder(department, score), 
                   xend = reorder(department, score),
                   y = 0, yend = score),
               linewidth = 1.5) +
  # Add points
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  # Add target reference line
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Flip coordinates for horizontal layout
  coord_flip() +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Above Target" = "#52A675", 
                                 "Below Target" = "#E76F51")) +
  # Format y-axis
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
                     limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Scores by Department",
    subtitle = "Dashed line shows company target (80 points)",
    x = "Department",
    y = "Satisfaction Score (0-100)",
    color = "Performance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

### Code Explanation

**Lines 2-6:** Creates a new column `performance` categorizing departments as "Above Target" or "Below Target"

**Lines 8-9:** `ggplot()` with `reorder(department, score)` to sort departments by score, and `color = performance` for conditional coloring

**Lines 11-15:** `geom_segment()` creates vertical lines with increased thickness (`linewidth = 1.5`)

**Line 17:** `geom_point()` adds larger points (size = 5)

**Lines 19-20:** `geom_hline()` adds a dashed horizontal reference line at the target score (80)

**Line 22:** `coord_flip()` rotates the chart to horizontal orientation for better department name readability

**Lines 24-25:** `scale_color_manual()` applies green for above target and coral for below target

**Lines 27-28:** `scale_y_continuous()` sets axis breaks and limits

**Lines 29-35:** `labs()` adds descriptive title, subtitle explaining the target line, and clear axis labels

**Line 36:** `theme_minimal()` applies clean theme

**Lines 37-40:** `theme()` customizes title and legend position

::: {.highlight-box .success}
**What we have now:**
A much more informative chart with sorted departments, color-coded performance, and a clear target reference. The horizontal orientation and clean formatting make it presentation-ready.
:::

## Chart 3: Advanced Visualization

Let's take it to the next level with enhanced styling, value labels, variance from target, and polished formatting suitable for publication.

::: {.highlight-box .warning}
**What we're adding in this final evolution:**

- **Variance indicators** showing distance from target
- **Value labels** on each point
- **Segment styling** from target line instead of zero
- **Enhanced color palette** with gradient effect
- **Department rankings** in labels
- **Summary statistics** annotation
- **Enhanced typography** with refined spacing
- **Data source caption** for proper attribution

:::

```{r}
#| label: chart-advanced
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

# Calculate variance from target and add rankings
target_value <- 80  # Store target as variable

data_satisfaction <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(
    variance = score - target_value,
    rank = rank(-score, ties.method = "first"),
    dept_label = paste0("#", rank, " ", department)
  )

# Calculate summary statistics
avg_score <- round(mean(data_satisfaction$score), 1)
above_target_pct <- round(sum(data_satisfaction$score >= target_value) / 
                          nrow(data_satisfaction) * 100, 0)

# Define enhanced color palette
perf_colors <- c("Above Target" = "#2E7D32", "Below Target" = "#C62828")

ggplot(data_satisfaction, aes(x = reorder(dept_label, score), y = score)) +
  # Draw segments from target line to score
  geom_segment(aes(x = reorder(dept_label, score), 
                   xend = reorder(dept_label, score),
                   y = target_value, yend = score,
                   color = performance),
               linewidth = 2,
               alpha = 0.8) +
  # Add target reference line
  geom_hline(yintercept = target_value, 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             color = "gray30", 
             linewidth = 1) +
  # Add points with enhanced styling
  geom_point(aes(color = performance), 
             size = 6,
             alpha = 0.9) +
  # Add value labels
  geom_text(aes(label = score),
            hjust = -0.5,
            size = 3.5,
            fontface = "bold",
            color = "gray20") +
  # Add variance labels
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(variance >= 0, 
                                paste0("+", variance), 
                                as.character(variance))),
            hjust = 1.5,
            size = 3,
            color = "gray40") +
  # Flip coordinates
  coord_flip() +
  # Apply custom colors
  scale_color_manual(values = perf_colors,
                     name = "vs Target (80)") +
  # Format x-axis (becomes y after flip)
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10),
                     limits = c(0, 95),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.15))) +
  # Add comprehensive labels
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Performance: 63% of Departments Meet Target",
    subtitle = "Technical leads with 88 points (+8 vs target) | Segments show variance from 80-point target",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Satisfaction Score (out of 100)",
    caption = "Data source: Q4 2024 Customer Satisfaction Survey | n = 1,247 responses | Visualization: Your Name"
  ) +
  # Add summary statistics as text annotation (no box, positioned at bottom right)
  annotate("text",
           x = 1, y = 90,
           label = paste0("Summary: Avg = ", avg_score, 
                         " | Above Target = ", above_target_pct, 
                         "% | Range = ", min(data_satisfaction$score), 
                         "-", max(data_satisfaction$score)),
           hjust = 0,
           size = 3.2,
           color = "gray30",
           fontface = "italic") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # Title and text styling
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16,
                              margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "#5A6C7D",
                                  lineheight = 1.3,
                                  margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#6C757D",
                                hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    
    # Axis styling
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold",
                              margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#2C3E50"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    
    # Legend styling
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    
    # Grid and panel styling
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#E9ECEF", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
    # Margins
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )
```

### Code Explanation

**Lines 2-7:** Calculates variance from target, ranking, and creates department labels with rank numbers

**Lines 10-12:** Calculates summary statistics including average score and percentage above target

**Line 15:** Defines enhanced color palette with darker, more professional shades

**Line 17:** `ggplot()` with reordered department labels including rankings

**Lines 19-26:** `geom_segment()` creates segments that start at the target line (80) rather than zero, making variance immediately visible. Color coded by performance with increased thickness

**Lines 28-31:** `geom_hline()` adds prominent target reference line

**Lines 33-35:** `geom_point()` adds large colored points

**Lines 37-41:** `geom_text()` adds score value labels to the right of points

**Lines 43-48:** `geom_text()` adds variance labels (e.g., "+8" or "-12") to the left of points

**Line 50:** `coord_flip()` for horizontal orientation

**Lines 52-53:** `scale_color_manual()` applies custom colors

**Lines 55-57:** `scale_y_continuous()` with expanded right margin for labels

**Lines 59-65:** `labs()` adds comprehensive labels including percentage meeting target in title, top performer in subtitle, and detailed caption

**Lines 67-93:** Multiple `annotate()` calls create a summary statistics box showing average, percentage above target, and score range

**Lines 94-122:** Comprehensive theme customization including enhanced typography, legend at top, grid customization, and proper margins

::: {.highlight-box .success}
**Final result:**
A publication-ready lollipop chart that clearly communicates satisfaction performance across departments. The segments starting from the target line, variance labels, ranking numbers, and summary statistics box create a comprehensive visualization suitable for executive presentations, reports, or dashboards.
:::

## Comparison: All Three Charts

Here's a side-by-side view of our progression:

| Aspect | Basic | Intermediate | Advanced |
|--------|-------|--------------|----------|
| **Readability** | Poor (unsorted, vertical) | Good (sorted, horizontal, colored) | Excellent (all + rankings + variance) |
| **Context** | None | Title & target line | Full context with summary stats |
| **Visual Appeal** | Plain points and lines | Color-coded with reference | Enhanced colors + annotations |
| **Data Layers** | Points only | Points + target line | Points + variance segments + labels |
| **Statistical Info** | Visual values only | Target comparison | Variance, rankings, summary stats |
| **Professional Use** | Not recommended | Acceptable for internal use | Publication-ready |

## Key Takeaways

::: {.callout-tip}
**Tips for Creating Better ggplot2 Lollipop Charts:**

1. **Always reorder categories** - Use `reorder()` to sort by value for easier visual comparison and pattern recognition

2. **Use horizontal orientation for long labels** - Apply `coord_flip()` when category names are lengthy or numerous

3. **Start segments meaningfully** - Instead of always starting at zero, consider starting from a baseline (like target or mean) to emphasize variance

4. **Add reference lines** - Use `geom_hline()` or `geom_vline()` to show targets, averages, or thresholds

5. **Color with purpose** - Use color to show categorical groups or highlight above/below threshold performance

6. **Label directly** - Add value labels with `geom_text()` to reduce need for axis reading, especially with many categories

7. **Adjust segment thickness** - Use `linewidth = 1.5-2.5` for segments; too thin looks fragile, too thick looks heavy

8. **Mind the point size** - Points should be 4-6 size units; large enough to see but not overwhelming

9. **Consider Cleveland dot plots** - For comparing multiple groups, consider faceting or using `geom_linerange()` with two points

10. **Export at high resolution** - Use `ggsave("plot.png", width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)` for publication-quality images

:::

## Next Steps

- **Slope charts** for visualizing trends across categories
- **Dot plots** with error bars for showing uncertainty
- **Cleveland dot plots** for multi-group comparisons

::: {.highlight-box .info}
**Want to create grouped lollipop charts?**

You can show multiple series with position dodging:

```r
# Create data with two time periods
data_comparison <- data_satisfaction %>%
  select(department, score) %>%
  rename(current = score) %>%
  mutate(previous = current - sample(-5:8, n(), replace = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(current, previous), 
               names_to = "period", 
               values_to = "score")

# Create grouped lollipop chart
ggplot(data_comparison, 
       aes(x = reorder(department, score), 
           y = score, 
           color = period)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, 
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = department, 
                   y = 0, yend = score),
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
               linewidth = 1) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2C5F8D", "#E76F51"),
                     labels = c("Current Quarter", "Previous Quarter")) +
  labs(title = "Satisfaction Score Comparison",
       x = "Department",
       y = "Score",
       color = "Period") +
  theme_minimal()
```

This creates side-by-side lollipops showing changes over time.
:::

## Alternative: Dumbbell Chart

Here's a bonus approach showing change between two points:

```{r}
#| label: bonus-dumbbell
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

# Create before/after data
data_dumbbell <- data_satisfaction %>%
  mutate(previous_score = score - sample(3:12, n(), replace = TRUE)) %>%
  select(department, previous_score, score, rank)

ggplot(data_dumbbell) +
  # Draw segments between points
  geom_segment(aes(x = previous_score, xend = score,
                   y = reorder(department, score), 
                   yend = reorder(department, score)),
               color = "gray70",
               linewidth = 2) +
  # Add previous period points
  geom_point(aes(x = previous_score, 
                 y = reorder(department, score)),
             color = "#E76F51",
             size = 5) +
  # Add current period points
  geom_point(aes(x = score, 
                 y = reorder(department, score)),
             color = "#52A675",
             size = 5) +
  # Add labels
  labs(
    title = "Customer Satisfaction Improvement by Department",
    subtitle = "All departments showed improvement from Q3 to Q4 2024",
    x = "Satisfaction Score",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```
